docRequirement: sub-agents.md:496 and :513-515 bind a subagent's `memory: user|project|local` to a real persistent directory — `~/.claude/agent-memory/<name-of-agent>/`, `.claude/agent-memory/<name-of-agent>/`, `.claude/agent-memory-local/<name-of-agent>/`. When it is set (and auto memory is not disabled, :517), three things MUST happen at spawn: :521 "The subagent's system prompt includes instructions for reading and writing to the memory directory."; :522 the prompt "also includes the first 200 lines or 25KB of `MEMORY.md` in the memory directory, whichever comes first, with instructions to curate `MEMORY.md` if it exceeds that limit"; :523 "Read, Write, and Edit tools are automatically enabled so the subagent can manage its memory files."
current: `memory` is parsed and strictly validated, carried on every definition shape, and then consumed by nothing. Type and the doc's own directory mapping: packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:38-44. Strict normalizer: definitions.ts:366-370, with a hard throw on a typo at :427-428 (`Invalid <label>.memory: expected user, project or local`). Consumption ends there. `grep -c -a 'memory' packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts` returns 0: the module that actually spawns a child never sees the field. `composeChildPrompt` (spawner.ts:305-312) is exactly `safety core + context seed + agentDef.systemPrompt` with no memory branch, and `allowedTools` (spawner.ts:295-297) is `agentDef.tools` minus `disallowedTools` with no force-enable. The fork DOES have a live memory subsystem, but it is a different one and is not keyed on this field: session/project/user `MEMORY.md` discovery in packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:13-27, the 200-line cap at :8, the prompt block at :139-141 and :317-334, the `remember` tool at packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.ts:7-10 and :51-59, and the master switch `getMemoryEnabled()` at packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:1104-1111 (the fork's `autoMemoryEnabled`). Those records reach a child only as the generic pinned capability memory (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/context-resource.ts:65-67, intersected at child-session-port.ts:188) — identical for every subagent, per-session not per-agent.
divergence: Not a key-name or value mismatch: the value is parsed correctly and the scope vocabulary matches the page exactly. The entire consumption half is absent. Missing, in order of the doc's three bullets: (1) no per-agent directory is derived or created for any of the three scopes, so :513-515 has no filesystem counterpart at all; (2) `composeChildPrompt` emits no read/write instruction block naming that directory (:521); (3) no `MEMORY.md` is read from it, so neither the 200-line nor the 25KB half of :522 exists — note `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` exists at memory-store.ts:8 but there is no byte cap anywhere, so even the reusable half is only half; (4) `read`/`write`/`edit` are not force-enabled (:523), which is the load-bearing one — the shipped read-only toolset is `['read','grep','find','ls']` (definitions.ts:157), so a `toolset: read-only` agent with `memory: project` is told to curate a file it has no tool to write. The field is silently inert rather than actively misleading only because the host never tells the agent it has memory; an author who follows the doc's own tip (sub-agents.md:529-532) and writes "update your agent memory" into the definition body does produce a subagent that has been told it has memory and cannot write it.

change.what: Add the per-agent layer next to the existing session/project/user helpers at :13-27. `export const AGENT_MEMORY_DIR = 'agent-memory'` and `AGENT_MEMORY_LOCAL_DIR = 'agent-memory-local'`; `getAgentMemoryDirPath(scope: AgentMemoryScope, agentName: string, opts: { workingDirectory?: string; configDir?: string })` mapping the doc's three rows onto Nessy paths — `user` -> join(CONFIG_DIR, 'agent-memory', name) (CONFIG_DIR = ~/.nessy-agent, config/paths.ts:18-21), `project` -> join(workingDirectory, NESSY_AGENT_PROJECT_DIR, 'agent-memory', name), `local` -> join(workingDirectory, NESSY_AGENT_PROJECT_DIR, 'agent-memory-local', name) (NESSY_AGENT_PROJECT_DIR = '.nessy-agent', packages/shared/src/projects/nessy-agent-layout.ts:12). Sanitize `agentName` to a single path segment (imported plugin agent keys contain ':' and '/'). Add `export const MEMORY_BYTE_LIMIT = 25 * 1024` — it does not exist today; `readMemoryFile` at :29-33 caps lines only, so give it an optional byte cap and stop at whichever limit hits first (:522 'whichever comes first'). Add `loadAgentMemoryPromptBlock(scope, agentName, opts)` returning '' when `getMemoryEnabled()` is false (:144-150 already wraps it as `isMemoryEnabled`), else mkdir the directory recursively and return a block that (a) names the absolute directory and instructs read+write, (b) inlines the capped `MEMORY.md`, (c) adds the curate-if-truncated instruction only when a cap actually truncated. Do NOT route this through `loadMemoryPromptBlock` (:317-334) — that one merges and dedups the session/user/project tier and would cross-contaminate per-agent memory.

Add `memory?: AgentMemoryScope` beside `skillKeys`/`mcpServerKeys` at :54-55, with the same 'omitted when unset so legacy child requests stay byte-identical' contract the neighbouring fields carry. This constant is 'byte-for-byte what orchestrator/spawner.ts:composeChildPrompt produces' and asserts at the RPC delivery boundary. Extend it with a memory case: an agent with `memory: project` must deliver a prompt containing the directory path and the MEMORY.md body; an agent without the field must stay byte-identical to today.

Two tests: a `toolset: read-only` + `memory: user` agent gets `read`/`write`/`edit` in `restrictions.tools` while `restrictions.worktreePolicy` stays `'shared'` (the toolset trap); and an agent with no `memory` produces a restrictions object byte-identical to today (no new key).

blastRadius: Crosses a wire AND a persistence boundary — an explicit risk trigger in this repo. `PiChildRestrictionsV1` is the host<->pi-subprocess child-start contract and is persisted verbatim inside `PiChildSessionRecordV1.restrictions` (child-session-port.ts:60-92), so a resumed or restarted child re-reads it; the new key must be optional and old records must parse unchanged. Readers of the restrictions object: spawner.ts:552-581 (producer), SessionManager.ts:10942-11136 (host validator/recomposer, which also clamps tools, maxTurns and permissionMode from the same literal), and `startPiChildRuntime`. Tool-list changes reach the child's permission gate: `inheritedTools` narrowing at SessionManager.ts:10993-10995, the skill `disallowedTools` chokepoint at :11004-11016, and `worktreePolicy` at spawner.ts:566-568 — widening the tool list without pinning `toolset` relocates the child's working tree. Definition-side readers already carrying the field and unaffected by shape: definitions.ts:454/:702, runtime-agent-definition.ts:371/:661, runtime-agent-definitions.ts:173. Filesystem: a new `.nessy-agent/agent-memory/` and `.nessy-agent/agent-memory-local/` under the project root — the local one needs a `.gitignore` entry, and neither is inside the containment set `native-sources.ts` scans (it reads only `.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md` at :1027), so per-agent files will not leak into the session capability view; confirm that is intended. Imported-plugin path: Claude plugin agents flow through `runtime-agent-definition.ts:616-620`, so plugin-supplied agent names (which contain ':' and '/') become directory names and must be sanitized. Existing tests touching the field: definitions.test.ts:101 and :178-187.
userImpact: Observable today. Author an agent with `memory: project` — in `orchestratorAgents` config, in `.nessy-agent/agents/<name>.md` frontmatter, or by importing a Claude plugin agent that uses the field — and it validates, round-trips and then behaves exactly as if the field were absent. No directory appears under `~/.nessy-agent/agent-memory/` or `.nessy-agent/`; run the agent twice and the second run has learned nothing; there is no warning, no debug line, no UI affordance saying memory is unsupported. The sharpest case is the one the doc's own example produces (sub-agents.md:499-509, a `code-reviewer` told in its body to 'update your agent memory'): with `toolset: read-only` the child's tools are `['read','grep','find','ls']`, so an agent that has been instructed to write its memory has no `write` or `edit` tool and either silently skips the instruction or burns a turn on an unavailable tool. Users importing Claude subagent bundles hit this without ever writing the field themselves.
